title: Shadow-traffic drift containment, telemetry contract fixes, and auto-rollback threshold tuning
creator: Maya Chen
description: After last week's rollout experiment we observed silent model drift that did not trigger the canary alarms. Root cause: gaps in the telemetry contract between shadow proxy and the metrics pipeline + overly permissive rollback hysteresis. This ticket tracks containment actions, telemetry contract fixes, adjustments to auto-rollback thresholds for A/B and canary runs, and a bounded experiment to validate the changes before the next release. Deliverables: (1) patch telemetry schemas + add schema validation in the proxy, (2) tighten rollback decision thresholds and add a low-latency fail-open guard, (3) expand shadow sampling for high-risk routes, (4) run an A/B validation job and update the runbook with specific signal checks and remediation steps.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry contract defined and enforced for shadow and canary events (schema validation in proxy + pipeline reject)
New rollback thresholds deployed (documented in runbook) and validated in 2 staged experiments without false positives >1%
Shadow sampling increased on three high-risk routes and load-tested to verify no svc degradation
Updated runbook published with playbook items, ownership, and automated checklist that can be executed in <10 minutes
PRs merged and e2e validation dashboards created (Grafana links in attachments)
comments: 2025-02-18 Maya Chen: Filed after triage call — observed 12% semantic drift on route /api/v1/generate that was only visible in trace logs. Early hypothesis: shadow requests missing key context tags, so aggregation skipped in downstream metrics. Refer to initial incident notes: https://drive.company.com/incident/2025-02-17-shadow-drift

2025-02-19 Diego Alvarez: Triage: mapped affected flows. Short-term mitigation: increase shadow-sample for route /api/v1/generate to 10% and publish emergency canary with 100 users to validate rollback path. Created hotfix branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/6789

2025-02-20 Priya Patel (PM): Noted customer impact is medium; customers saw increased hallucination on a small subset but no PII leakage. Agreed prioritization with SRE to avoid noisy alerts during fix rollout.

2025-02-22 Liam O'Connor (SRE): Found that the metrics pipeline drops events lacking 'model_variant' tag. Added schema validation test in CI and failing test reproducing missing-tag behavior: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1122

2025-02-25 Diego Alvarez: Prototype enforcement added to shadow proxy — proxy now attaches model_variant and request_hash. Deployed to staging. Load test results attached. Link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/staged/telemetry-checks

2025-02-27 Maya Chen: Runbook draft updated with step-by-step rollback checklist, signal definitions (per-token latency, semantic-similarity delta, error-rate delta) and ownership. PR: https://confluence.company.com/display/INF/Runbook+-+Shadow+and+Canary+Failures

2025-03-03 Diego Alvarez: Began staged A/B validation: 5k synthetic queries against baseline and candidate. Initial signals: semantic-similarity delta measured but alarm threshold triggered late because of 10m aggregation window. Action: add 30s rolling window for semantic-similarity check in canary pipeline. See experiment dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/ab/ab-2025-03-03

2025-03-04 Priya Patel: PM review completed. Agreed to reduce rollback hysteresis from 5% to 3% for semantic drift and to require two corroborating signals (latency or error-rate) before full rollback. Security sign-off requested for telemetry changes.
decisions: Enforce telemetry contract in proxy and fail-fast to avoid silent drops; pipeline will surface violations as alerts
Reduce semantic-drift rollback threshold from 5% to 3% and require 2 independent signals to trigger automatic rollback
Introduce a 30s rolling window for semantic similarity checks to reduce alerting latency
Increase shadow sampling to 10% for 3 high-risk routes during the validation window; if CPU increases >8% revert sampling
Add a temporary 'safe-mode' that routes failed validation candidate traffic to reduced-rate fallback model while leaving baseline unaffected
runbook_changes: Add 'telemetry contract verification' step that runs schema-validator and fails the canary if >0.1% events violate
Document exact signal definitions: semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), per-token latency p95, error-rate (4xx/5xx ratio)
Include escalation path to SRE + ML Eng with on-call runbook snippets and playbook for 'silent drift'
Add commands to increase/decrease shadow sampling and safe-mode activation CLI snippets
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1122 - telemetry: schema validation and CI checks
retrospective_notes: Telemetry contract gaps are the primary root cause; make contract verification part of pre-rollout gating
Overly-wide hysteresis delayed mitigation — balance between noisy rollbacks and silent regressions requires measurable risk budgets per-route
Shadow traffic sampling should be workload-aware: use adaptive sampling instead of global percentage
Add automated synthetic regressions as a pre-deploy step for model variants that are highly coupled to prompt templates
risk_mitigation: Guardrails: fail-open to baseline for unknown telemetry violations; safe-mode routing for degraded candidate models
Monitoring: short-window checks and multi-signal corroboration to avoid single-signal flapping
Operational: clear ownership and <10-minute playbook to contain an escalating drift event
Deployment: run A/B validation with synthetic traffic and limited real traffic before ramping to full canary
